extension.summary: Starfleet - TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Radio, Adult
extension.description: All-in-one Kodi plugin. TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Free Streaming, Adult (PIN-protected), Radio. Torrent/debrid sources via Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox. Elementum support for magnet playback.
extension.news:
v2.3.287 - Restored Radio to the main navigation â€” it had been fully working on the backend this whole time (country/state/city/station browsing, search, playback) but got orphaned from the UI once the custom Home skin replaced the native menu that used to list it, so there was no way to actually reach it anymore. Added a Radio button to the nav bar and built the same three-panel browsing flow (with the themed dialogs) the rest of the addon already has: countries -> states/provinces -> cities -> stations, quick-access country shortcuts, and search â€” all backed by the exact same resolution and playback logic as before, just with a way to get to it again. v2.3.286 - Themed three more native Kodi dialogs to match the rest of the addon (navy/orange, Starfleet icon) instead of whatever the user's active system skin looks like: the "Choose source"/stream picker (previously the native blue-highlight select list), and the busy spinner shown while browsing Adult movies (previously Kodi's default spinner). Both are real WindowXMLDialog replacements built the same way the progress dialog was last release, since native dialogs are rendered by the active system skin and can't be branded through the addon's own bundled skin folder otherwise. v2.3.285 - Fixed AllDebrid, Real-Debrid, Premiumize, and TorBox magnet resolution: AllDebrid and Real-Debrid's own bulk cache-check endpoints are both confirmed dead/unreliable now, which meant enabling either service still silently fell through to Elementum regardless of whether a torrent was actually cached - fixed by relying on each service's real add/upload attempt as the cache check instead (verified live end-to-end against AllDebrid with a real account and a real magnet). The second-chance magnet resolver used by Movies/TV/Adult playback only supported Real-Debrid and AllDebrid before - a Premiumize- or TorBox-only setup would skip straight to Elementum even with debrid enabled; now all four services are tried, in the priority order set in Settings. Confirmed the full chain is correct end to end: every enabled debrid service is tried before Elementum for movies, TV, and Adult magnets, and Elementum runs immediately with no added delay when no debrid service is enabled. Sports: added the missing Soccer icon (was still using a generic remote icon) and confirmed the full custom icon set is present. Movies/TV: added custom icons for the Action, Adventure, Animation, Comedy, Crime, and Documentary genre lists (other genres unchanged). v2.3.225 - Sports: fixed several menu/listing issues confirmed live tonight. TotalSportek24 (tstek) events always showed no LIVE tag regardless of actual status - was hardcoded false; now derived from whether the event's start time has recently passed (combat-sports cards run long, so a 5h window is used). UFC/Boxing/WWE/Tennis events with no parseable date from TheSportsDB now show "TBD" instead of a blank time, and one malformed record from that API can no longer blank out the rest of that day's events. NHL Network: onhockey.tv's own pages now gate the real player behind a nested same-domain iframe a single-page scrape can't follow (confirmed live - neither the dedicated page nor the old daddylive-wrapper page expose an extractable stream anymore) - switched to the same daddylive.mov channel-id resolver already used elsewhere. MLB Network: root-caused a real 403/no-stream failure to one mirror host (cdnlivetv.tv) using a new obfuscation scheme - the stream URL is split into ~10 separately base64-encoded fragments assembled by an in-page JS function, not the single XOR blob this resolver already handled - added a decoder for it and verified live it now returns a real, playable #EXTM3U playlist. Also fixed a filter bug in the debrid torrent-search path that could silently drop a legitimate movie/TV torrent if its uploader's display name happened to contain ".com" (e.g. an embedded site tag) - that string was incorrectly treated the same as a real non-video file extension (.exe/.zip/etc). Removed a leftover duplicate, unused search_torrentio() definition. (Investigated a report of Elementum/magnet playback being broken by this update - confirmed both the magnet-search and Elementum hand-off code are unchanged and correct; the specific case reported was simply an episode that hadn't been released yet, so no torrents existed anywhere for it yet.) v2.3.224 - Added a "Clear cache" button (Settings, top of the debrid/resolver section) - explains a real discrepancy found live tonight (Windows showed the new CFL menu entry, the same device's Firestick didn't): the Sports category list is cached 24h, and updating the addon's code doesn't invalidate an already-cached result from before the update - a device that browsed Sports earlier keeps serving the old list for the rest of that window regardless of version. Android also blocks ADB/file-manager access to the addon's own private data directory, so there was no way to force this without the app itself doing it - this button does it from inside Kodi's own Settings UI, no ADB or file access needed. v2.3.223 - Fixed a regression from v2.3.220's Adult title-cleaning: the bare word "XXX" was being stripped out of every title anywhere it appeared, but that word is frequently a real, intentional part of adult film titles (e.g. "The Odyssey: A XXX Parody" - a parody title genre convention), not junk. Stripping it mangled the title before it was used to cross-reference the real catalog for high-quality cover art, so that lookup stopped matching and posters fell back to nothing - confirmed live. Now only strips "XXX" when it's clearly its own bracketed tag, e.g. "(XXX)" or "[XXX]" with nothing else inside, which doesn't collide with a title that legitimately contains the word. v2.3.222 - Fixed Adult section listings collapsing to almost nothing after a few hours of real use (confirmed live: New Releases went from showing real content to showing none at all). Root cause was in the has-a-source filter added in v2.3.220: it decided whether to hide a title based on a passive index of whatever detail pages happened to already be cached from past browsing - early on that index is empty (lenient, shows everything), but after enough browsing it becomes non-empty while still being nowhere near a complete picture, and the filter started treating "never actually checked" the same as "confirmed no source", hiding almost everything. Fixed at the source: added a real, separate "confirmed no source" record that's only written after an actual search for that exact title comes back empty, and the filter now only hides a title once that's genuinely happened - titles it hasn't gotten to yet keep showing immediately like before, and only get hidden once really confirmed absent, so the list starts accurate and gets more accurate over time instead of collapsing. Also found (separate issue, not yet fixed): Adult DVD Empire's movie trailers are dead through this addon's existing trailer URL formula - checked a real, current film page directly and that entire domain/path pattern doesn't exist anymore; the site has moved trailers to a different domain requiring a per-scene ID this addon doesn't currently track, not just a movie ID. Needs its own scraper work to properly fix - flagged for a follow-up rather than a rushed fix tonight. v2.3.221 - EMERGENCY FIX: v2.3.220's bytecode-only build completely broke the addon - confirmed live via kodi.log that every single plugin:// call failed with "ImportError: bad magic number in 'resources'". The bytecode was correctly compiled for Python 3.11.9 (verified before shipping), but Kodi's own bundled Python 3.11 build on this device uses a different internal magic number stamp than standalone Python 3.11.9 - the exact version-mismatch risk flagged before attempting this, just at a finer-grained level (same Kodi major version, different bundled interpreter patch) than expected. Reverted immediately to plain, uncompiled source - identical code to v2.3.220, just not bytecode-compiled - to restore a working addon. No further obfuscation attempts until a build approach can be verified against Kodi's actual bundled interpreter directly rather than a same-numbered standalone Python install. v2.3.220 - Fixed CFL (and College Football/CFB) missing from the Sports menu entirely: confirmed live that CFL games were showing up with nowhere to actually navigate to them, because a dedup check meant to stop TheSportsDB's raw sport list from adding a redundant generic "American Football" menu entry was also (wrongly) applied to this addon's OWN curated category list - since NFL, CFB, and CFL are all classified as the same TheSportsDB sport ("American Football"), and NFL happens to be listed first, CFB and CFL were being silently skipped out of the menu every time, as if they didn't exist. Also fixed the actual cause of CFL games showing up mixed into the NFL listing itself (confirmed live: a real CFL game and a European League of Football game both appeared inside NFL) - the supplementary schedule source has no per-league split for American football, so it was merged in unfiltered for whichever of NFL/CFB/CFL happened to have a menu entry; now filtered by each game's real league name before merging, so NFL only shows NFL, CFL only shows CFL, etc. Both bugs together also explain why a real CFL game's own stream links weren't found when played from the (wrong) NFL section - the wrong sport was being passed to every stream resolver, none of which know to check CFL's actual listings when told to look for NFL. Fixed a narrow but real race condition behind the home screen occasionally failing to load a section on the first click (confirmed live, matched reports it "works on retry"): a background thread that pushes freshly-loaded data into the home screen can land mid-navigation and throw against an already-closing window; tightened from both sides so the window signals it's closing before doing anything else, and the background thread re-checks immediately before touching it. Also fixed the Sports section's page title showing a broken/unreadable placeholder character in the breadcrumb (e.g. "Videos / Starfleet / [?] Boxing") - a stadium/hockey emoji in the category title that this Kodi build's skin font can't render; replaced with plain text. Adult section: film titles are now cleaned of common scraping junk (duplicate year tags, resolution/release tags) before being displayed or used to check for a stream source - a mismatched messy title on one side of that check could cause a real, working film to be wrongly dropped as "no source"; the New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers listings were also found to skip the has-a-source check entirely (unlike every other Adult listing), so titles with no actual stream anywhere were shown and dead-ended on click - now filtered the same as everywhere else. Performer/actor search in the Adult section's unified search was a stub that always returned nothing ("no actor search API - skip for now") - built a real one backed by a cached full name index from the site's own per-letter actor pages. New sports stream source added (livetv902.me / livetv.sx family): covers a wide range of sports and leagues this addon didn't have a source for before; found via live investigation that its "alieztv"-type mirrors resolve through a plain, unobfuscated JS call to a real HLS URL - no WASM/P2P wall like embed.st - verified against a real live CFL game. Note: this source's availability was inconsistent in testing (worked reliably in some passes, not in others, without a clear cause) - it's wired in as a supplementary source alongside everything else, so it simply contributes nothing extra when it's not available rather than causing any problem. v2.3.219 - Fixed MLB Network and NHL Network (24/7 channels) not playing: verified live that daddylive.mov's signing CDN (fiveo4.casadenoval.uk) started rejecting every request with a bare 403, even a freshly-decoded, correctly-signed, not-yet-expired URL with the right Referer - this looked at first like the same un-fixable TLS-fingerprint wall documented elsewhere in this changelog for Cloudflare Turnstile, but confirmed by direct testing it isn't: the CDN now also requires the Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site "fetch metadata" headers a real browser always sends and that neither our scraper nor, importantly, Kodi's own player ever did - simply adding them (both to our own verification check and onto the URL Kodi's player actually opens, via the same header pipe-syntax already used elsewhere for Referer/User-Agent) resolves it. Also added a live-verification step this resolver was missing entirely: previously, once a mirror's obfuscated blob decoded into something that merely looked like a URL, that URL was handed straight to Kodi's player with no check that it would actually serve - now it's fetched and confirmed to return a real #EXTM3U playlist first, so a mirror that decodes but 403s (this exact bug) or serves an expired/dead link gets correctly skipped in favor of the next mirror instead of crashing playback. v2.3.218 - Fixed Adult section kicking the user all the way out of the addon on click, same class of bug as the Sports crash-out fixed in v2.3.216/217, but guaranteed to happen every time instead of intermittently: entering the Adult section shows a PIN entry prompt if one is set, and that prompt was popping up in the middle of the same window-activation sequence a Sports click goes through - any blocking dialog shown at that exact moment can make Kodi abandon the transition. The PIN check now happens before the home screen even starts navigating away, not during it. Also fixed a related bug found while fixing this: the "only ask for the PIN once per session" behavior never actually worked, because this addon runs with reuselanguageinvoker off (a fresh Python process per call, confirmed in addon.xml) - the old code stored the unlock flag in a plain in-memory variable that reset on every single click, silently re-prompting for the PIN every time despite the setting's own description promising otherwise. Now persisted properly so it actually only asks once. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is noticeably larger now - the previous release's ~2% bump turned out to be too subtle to see; also enlarged the matching per-row focus borders (there were two overlapping highlight mechanisms in the skin, only one of which was resized last time). v2.3.217 - Follow-up to v2.3.216's navigation fix, based on further live testing on the Firestick: the previous release stopped the "kicked all the way out of the addon" symptom, but a deeper live test showed the fix's own two-step handoff (jump to an empty placeholder screen first, then swap in the real category a moment later) could still get stuck - the second step silently failing to fire, leaving the user stranded on a permanently empty screen instead of the Sports (or Movies/TV/Live TV/Adult) page they clicked. Replaced that two-step handoff with a single direct jump straight to the clicked category, removing the fragile middle step entirely. Trade-off: Back out of a category may now return to Kodi's previous screen instead of this addon's home screen in some cases, rather than a category that may not load at all - confirmed working live against Sports. v2.3.216 - Fixed a real crash-on-navigate bug found by live-testing on the Firestick: clicking Sports (or any top-nav category) in the home screen could silently kick the user all the way out of the addon back to Kodi's own Add-ons screen, with no error dialog. Also: the dependency-check prompt (offers to install ResolveURL) was re-running on every single in-app navigation click, not just on first launch - could pop a blocking install prompt mid-navigation for no reason connected to what was actually clicked; now only runs when Home is genuinely (re)launching. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is now slightly larger (~2%) per user request, for better visibility. v2.3.215 - Fixed three real skin-navigation bugs found by live-testing on the Firestick with ADB: (1) an unprompted auto-relaunch, where backing all the way out to Kodi's own Add-ons screen would spontaneously reopen Starfleet's home a moment later with zero input - root cause was the addon's own root action relaunching Home on ANY visit to its plugin:// root with no fresh lock file present, including background metadata queries from Kodi/the active Kodi skin (e.g. Add-ons tile widgets), not just genuine user launches; now only relaunches when the Videos window is actually the one on screen. (2) The home screen's hero banner (title/plot/Play/More Info) could get stuck showing a previous section's item when switching to a section with no content yet (e.g. Live TV with no favorites saved) - it's now cleared instead of left stale. (3) Moving left/right at the very edge of a carousel row could unexpectedly jump focus to the top nav bar instead of stopping at the row - the row lists were missing their own left/right wrap targets, letting Kodi's automatic proximity navigation take over.
v2.3.214 - Added a new working stream resolver: streame.center, a shared embed backend used by several front-end sites (e.g. powerstreams.site, realsportshd.buzz) that a raw embed link alone can't play (its ch##.php/hls.php pages need a decrypt.php exchange first, done automatically now) - verified live against a real MLB game. Rather than write one scraper per front-end site (most of them have no real schedule of their own to scrape - one 403s outright, another is just a static link directory), this runs as a universal post-processing step across every existing source (StreamsEast, CrackStreams, etc), so any sport those sources already cover gets this fix automatically the moment one of them happens to route through streame.center. Also fixed the repo's own landing page (index.html) linking to a stale repository.starfleet-1.0.11.zip instead of the current 1.0.13 - a fresh install via that page was pulling the old repository add-on even though addons.xml itself was already correct.
v2.3.213 - Fixed CrackStreams returning 0 events for every sport, every time: its event-listing page was being fetched at /league/mlbstreams (etc.), which is a 404 - the site moved to /category/mlb/ (etc.) a while back, and even that correct page no longer has any scrapable per-game links in its static HTML (JS-rendered listing, like most of this ecosystem now). Rather than reverse-engineer another discovery API, this now builds the event page URL directly from the two team names in the title (CrackStreams' own URL pattern is the predictable /stream/<team>-vs-<team>, tried in both team orders) - verified live against a real game that this correctly finds the page and extracts its actual stream list, where before it always found nothing. Note: depending on the specific event, CrackStreams' own links may route through the same embed.st-family WASM-gated hosts documented as unfixable in previous releases - that's a limitation of whichever embed provider that event happens to use, not of this fix.
v2.3.212 - New working stream source for MLB/NBA/NHL/NFL: mlb24all.ir and its sibling sites (nba24all.ir, nhl24all.ir, nfl24all.ir) were already listed in this addon's own code as a planned source, but the implementation was dead - it scraped for HTML anchor links that stopped existing once those sites became client-rendered apps, and it was never actually wired into the stream picker to begin with. Replaced it with a real implementation found via live network inspection: these sites run a clean, unauthenticated JSON API (GET .../api/v3/stateshot for the game/team catalogue, POST .../api/v2/generate_stream_info for a direct playable HLS link) - no login, no obfuscation, no WASM, just a straightforward API call. Verified live against an in-progress Blue Jays vs Rays game: returns real, independently-confirmed-working ESPN Home/Away broadcast links. This runs alongside every other source in the same merged link dialog, so a game covered by this source now shows up as extra "Link N" options next to StreamsEast/DaddyLive/etc.
v2.3.211 - Fixed a real crash-on-play bug found by testing the Blue Jays game live on-device: the DaddyLive/TVNow24/7-channel resolver (used for the MLB/NHL Network channels and as the supplementary source merged into every sport event's link dialog) would, when none of a channel's mirrors could be decoded, hand back the raw unresolved mirror page URL on the theory that ResolveURL "might know it" â€” instead Kodi got a plain HTML page and crashed immediately with "error probing input format". Now returns nothing for that channel instead, so it's correctly dropped from the dialog rather than offered as a guaranteed-broken option. Also discovered and wired up a much more reliable resolution path for one whole class of these mirrors: some daddylive.mov mirrors point at tvnow247.top's own /embed/<channel> page, which used to fail outright (it's a client-rendered app with nothing scrapable in its HTML) â€” found via live network inspection that its player calls a clean JSON API (chat.cfbu247.sbs/api/resolve-dlstream) to get its real stream, so that's tried first now, with a live-playlist check before accepting it (a couple of channels' upstreams turned out to be genuinely offline right now, verified directly â€” not a scraper bug, just those specific feeds being down). StreamsEast (embed.st) links are confirmed to depend on a WASM+P2P ticket-exchange system with no static stream URL anywhere in the page - verified via live browser inspection that even a real browser only gets a playable stream after running embed.st's own obfuscated code, which can't be replicated from a Kodi Python addon - left as-is this release since that's a limitation of that specific host, not something scraping can fix.
v2.3.210 - Fixed MLB (and every sport's) StreamsEast source: streamseast.is is dead (the domain no longer resolves at all); the site moved to streameasti.is with a different URL structure (no numeric event id, irregular section-name pluralization) and a different embed mechanism (source buttons carry a base64-encoded URL in a data-s attribute, swapped into the player by a JS click handler â€” the iframe's own src is always blank in the raw HTML, so the old scraper found nothing). Updated the domain, URL patterns, and added the data-s extraction, so StreamsEast now contributes real "Link N" options again for every sport, not just MLB. Verified against a real live Blue Jays game: get_event_streams now returns 3 StreamsEast links + 3 more from the TVNow247/DaddyLive source added in v2.3.209, all 6 shown together in one sequentially-numbered dialog (this merging was already automatic â€” fixing the two sources was the actual work). v2.3.209 - New: MLB Network 24/7 channel added to the MLB section â€” selecting it shows a Link 1/2/3 picker across three known-good daddylive.mov mirrors. New: full Live TV source added â€” TVNow247 (500+ channels scraped from tvnow247.top, adult channels excluded). New: live sports events scraped from tvnow247.top/schedule.json are now merged into each sport's event listing and used as a supplementary stream source everywhere, categorized by sport automatically. Fixed a real bug found while building these: the daddylive.mov channel resolver assumed every mirror-list JSON entry has the same {name,url} shape, but some pages use {name,id,url} with an extra field in between â€” entries in that shape were silently never matching. Also fixed: numeric-only channel ids (this addon's own MLB "399" test case, plus most of TVNow247's catalogue) were falling back to parsing the page's title tag for the real channel name, but title formats vary wildly ("Free X Live...", "Watch X Online...", "X Live Stream Free...") and that guess was unreliable â€” callers that already know the real name (the new TV channel list, the new events scraper) now pass it through explicitly instead of guessing, which took random-sample channel resolution from 0% to 100% in testing. v2.3.208 - v2.3.207 verified live: NHL Network now resolves and plays (confirmed reaching video decode), and Back from Movies/TV Shows/etc now correctly returns to the home screen. This release fixes the one remaining piece: the carousel focus highlight still wasn't showing, because the id=90 overlay control had a hardcoded <visible>false</visible> in the skin XML â€” Kodi re-evaluates XML visible conditions continuously, which silently overrides/no-ops any Python setVisible(True) call. Removed the XML condition; visibility is now owned entirely by home.py (explicitly hidden on init, shown/positioned on focus). v2.3.207 - NHL Network 24/7 channel still didn't play after v2.3.205's onhockey.tv fix, because onhockey.tv's own proxy for that channel (daddylive.php) is dead (404). Now resolves directly via daddylive.mov's channel mirror list, decoding the obfuscated embed script one mirror tier uses to get a fresh signed .m3u8. Also: fixed Adult section movie posters occasionally showing a neighboring film's cover art (nearest-match bug in the cover-art scraper). Also: home screen carousel focus highlight (the orange selection border on Movies/TV/etc rows) now actually renders â€” it was never appearing on some devices/Kodi builds even though selection itself worked. Also: Back from a section (Movies/TV Shows/etc) now correctly returns to the home screen instead of exiting past the addon into Kodi's own Videos section. v2.3.206 - Fix free/non-debrid streams not resolving: script.module.resolveurl was marked optional and pinned to a stale version (5.1.28) that was never actually hosted anywhere, so it was silently never installed. Now required, bumped to the real published 5.1.206, and pulled from the repository's new smrzips repo dir. v2.3.205 - Fix NHL Network (Sports section) not playing: onhockey.tv's live-channel page (used for the 24/7 NHL Network stream) embeds its player via JS config (src/file/source: "...m3u8") or a same-domain proxy iframe, not the plain stream links the scraper was looking for. Added JS-embedded m3u8 detection and a same-domain iframe follow-through, matching the extraction already used successfully for this exact channel in the Live TV section.

Elementum is a torrent finding and streaming engine. It doesn't go on torrent websites for legal reasons. However, it calls specially crafted add-ons (called providers) that are installed separately. This project is a fork of the well known, but no longer maintained Pulsar/Quasar projects from steeve and scakemyer. NOTE: install plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.zip from the repository first, then manually install the matching plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.<platform>.zip on top for your device's platform (e.g. windows_x64, android_arm64, linux_x64) and restart Kodi - binaries are split into per-platform zips to stay under GitHub's 100MB file size limit.
